VIVARIUM — DESIGN MARKUPS
What to cut, what to add. Left column is the app as it is today, recreated from src/. Right column is the proposal. Both at 390px.

CUT — delete it. The information is duplicated, or it does not change what you do next.
MERGE / TRIM / SWAP — keep the information, spend less screen on it.
NEW — add it. In every case here the data already exists in the app and never reaches a screen.

The thread running through all three screens: the app tells you a lot about state, and very little about what to do about it — and it tells you the same state three or four times per screen.

The second page, Mobile vs web, takes this proposal to 1440px.

DASHBOARD

Cut
· "Fed this week" stat card — punishes long feeding cycles
· The whole-collection photo grid — it is the Animals tab, and it renders every animal
· The three mini stats at the bottom — all three live on Stats

Merge
· "Needs feeding" + "Due soon" → one queue ordered by lateness

Add
· A workload line under the greeting
· Last meal on each queue row, so Feed can prefill
· Medication doses in the queue — medication_schedules is modelled and never rendered
· Select → batch log for the queue
· Low feeder stock, before you start feeding

Net: roughly 1720px of scroll down to about 1280, and the part you act on fits on one screen.

ANIMALS

Cut
· The urgent carousel — the third rendering of the overdue list, sitting on top of the search box
· Streak badge and tag chips on the card

Change
· "Fed 18 days ago" → "4 days overdue". 18 days is fine for one animal and late for another; only the schedule knows which.

Add
· Status filter chips — you can sort by overdue today, but not filter to it, and quarantine is invisible
· Grid / list density toggle — the photo grid is lovely at 12 animals and unusable at 50
· Enclosure on the card

Open question: is the Enclosures tab pulling its weight where it is, or is it really a grouping of this list?

ANIMAL PROFILE

This screen states "this animal is late" three times in the top 400px: the header chip, the banner, and the Next feeding tile.

Cut
· The header chip row — all three chips repeat the stats grid below, with less in them
· The overdue banner
· Two tabs: Feeding and Vitals are Timeline with a filter chip pre-selected

Add
· One feeding bar carrying status + last meal + the only Feed button
· Enclosure under the name
· "Takes food — 9 of 10", already computed on the Feeding tab, promoted to a tile
· Weight sparkline on its tile
· Health as the third quick action

Nothing is deleted from the data — the Feeding and Vitals tabs' contents are already reachable through Timeline's filters.

MOBILE VS WEB
The same proposal at both widths, and the rules that connect them. Phone boards on the left, web on the right.

What exists today: the app's whole responsive treatment is four things — card grids go 2 to 3 to 4 columns, the bottom padding drops (md:pb-8, in six files), the FAB hides, and the sidebar appears. Seven breakpoint utilities in Dashboard, seven in AnimalDetail, five in Animals, one each everywhere else. There is no desktop layout; there is a phone layout centred in a max-w-5xl column with 96px of dead gutter on each side.

The answer is not a separate web design — it is one set of components that know what to do with more width. Board 1 shows the problem. The two pairs below show the same screen at both sizes. "How a row folds" traces every field between the two arrangements, and the last board is the spec.

TODAY AT 1440px

Three things break, and none of them are cosmetic.

1. Rows stretch instead of filling. A queue row spans 1024px with a 10px dot at one end and a 12px button at the other. The fields that would justify that width — the schedule, the last meal, the enclosure — are not shown at any width.

2. The stat grid is grid-cols-2 with no breakpoint at all: two 506px cards, each holding a single digit.

3. Four actions disappear. The FAB offers add animal, feeding, shed, weight and expense; it is md:hidden, and its desktop replacement is one Log feeding button. Above 768px, logging a shed or a weight means opening an animal first.

The photo grid is the one thing that genuinely responds.

DASHBOARD, BOTH WIDTHS

The phone board is not a smaller web board — it is the same components with the queue rows folded and the rail unrolled into the flow.

What differs, and why
· Queue rows: columns on the web, two lines on the phone. Every field survives except the species subtitle.
· Stock and activity: a 380px rail on the web; on the phone, stock stays directly under the queue it affects and activity follows.
· Trigger for the five log actions: FAB on the phone, split button on the web.

What does not differ
The queue's order, the workload line, the 44px targets, the tokens, and every action and destination.

The bottom nav here is five tabs, not the four in the app today — see the parity board.

PROFILE, BOTH WIDTHS

One relationship carries this pair: the phone's top stack — photo, identity, enclosure, feeding bar, quick actions, stats — IS the desktop's 380px rail. On the web it pins to the left and stays put while you read the history; on the phone it is simply the top of the screen and scrolls away.

That is why the mobile profile needed no separate design. Fix the stack once and both widths improve.

Records fold rather than truncate: the phone row gains result and who logged it, which it does not show today. Only free-text notes go behind the tap.

Charts: sparkline in the tile on a phone, full chart inline on the web. The profile is capped at max-w-3xl today, so that cap has to rise for the two-column layout.

PARITY AND THE FOLD

These two boards are the load-bearing claims of the whole page, drawn rather than asserted.

Parity — the sidebar's six destinations arrive on a phone as four, so Feeding and Stats cannot be reached at all; and the FAB's five actions arrive on the web as one. Both are fixed by changing the trigger, not the capability: five tabs plus a More sheet, and a split button carrying the same five actions in the same order.

The fold — numbers trace each field between the desktop and phone arrangements. Six of six queue fields and six of seven record fields survive. The rule it generalises to: compose fields into phrases, demote only the unbounded one, and never make a phone row a mystery you have to tap to resolve.

WHEN NOTHING IS DUE
The proposal on page 2 is built entirely from exceptions — a queue of what is late, a warning when stock is low, a feed of what just happened. On a well-run collection with 14-day cycles, none of those fire on most days, so the dashboard would be close to blank. That is a real hole in it, and this page closes it.

The principle: the layout does not restructure between states. Four slots stay put; their heading and fill change. The queue does not vanish when it empties — it widens its horizon from today to the next seven days. And the space that opens up goes to husbandry that is always true but never urgent: unscheduled animals, stale weights, predicted sheds, running quarantines.

Before any of that, though, read the red box on the states board — the app currently cannot tell an all-clear collection from one that has never been fed.

THE ALL-CLEAR DASHBOARD

Four changes from the busy version, no new structure.

1. The confirmation is one clause in the workload line — "Nothing due today · next is Monty, Thursday". Not a banner, not a tick, not a celebration. This is the normal state, so it cannot cost a card.

2. The queue widens rather than empties: "Today" becomes "Coming up", the next 7 days, and the Feed button gives way to a date because nothing is actionable yet.

3. "Worth a look" appears — husbandry that is never urgent and so never surfaces. Capped at four rows, and it yields completely when there is a queue.

4. Stock becomes a projection: schedules give the burn rate, so it answers "will I run out?" rather than only shouting once you have.

Nothing here is invented to fill space — every row is a fact about the collection that is true on a busy day too, just outranked.

THE STATE LADDER

Five states, and the app can currently distinguish three of them.

The one to fix regardless of any redesign: getStatusForAnimal returns 'muted' when an animal has no last_fed_at or no feeding_frequency_days, and the overdue tally counts only 'red'. So an animal with no schedule never appears in any queue, ever — and a twelve-animal collection that has never been fed shows "Overdue 0" in green.

The healthiest-looking state and the least-known state render identically. An all-clear message is only honest once the dashboard can tell them apart, which is why "3 animals have no feeding schedule" is the first row of Worth a look rather than a nicety.

The two states the app cannot see are both quiet ones. That is the answer to the question: it should be able to say it is genuinely up to date, not merely that it has nothing to say.
